extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and proof-assistant developers interested in formal proof compilation (Lean 4 / Coq) and auditability
extracted.subtask_description: Deterministic compilation of proof traces from the Braid Theorem Prover into Lean 4 and Coq syntax, with emphasis on auditability, portability, and reviewability by the mathematician community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deterministically compiles proof traces from the Phase 11 Braid Theorem Prover into Lean 4 and Coq syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinism was verified across 26 tests (page claims determinism verified across 26 tests). The implementation is the Phase 17 Lean Formal Compiler (STEP 564) intended to produce the same output given the same input proof trace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Braid -> Lean 1:1 syntactic compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Braid -> Lean 1:1 syntactic compilation, exploiting structural isomorphism between Reidemeister moves R1/R2/R3 and Lean rewrite tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compiler aims for a syntactic, one-to-one mapping that preserves the structure of braid-prover steps by mapping Reidemeister moves directly to Lean rewrite tactics, i.e., preserve structural isomorphism rather than performing semantic re-proving or heavy transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coq portability bridge (same AST emits both provers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coq portability bridge: the same AST emits both Lean and Coq, demonstrating two-prover portability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single abstract syntax tree (AST) is used as the emitter backend so that the same proof trace can be emitted as both Lean and Coq source, evidencing portability between provers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProofCertificate auditability (fingerprint + metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofCertificate auditability: REI-LEAN-xxxxxxxx fingerprint + metadata to enable auditing of compiled proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates include a fingerprint (example format REI-LEAN-xxxxxxxx) plus metadata so auditors can verify provenance and identity of proofs; the artifact claims determinism across tests to aid reproducible auditing.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-to-end demonstration on example braid samples
rubrics_metrics.description: End-to-end demonstration on 4 braid samples with concrete outputs: total Lean 115 lines, Coq 130 lines, all fingerprints unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implementation is validated with concrete examples (4 braid samples), reporting output sizes and uniqueness of fingerprints as evidence of end-to-end functionality and non-collision of certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability and honest presentation to the mathematician community
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest sequel to previous work explicitly noting the need for review by the mathematician community; emphasis on providing an 'honest bridge' for mathematicians to review compiled proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project frames itself as seeking review and audit by mathematicians (addressing prior paper's noted need). This implies criteria of transparency, sufficient documentation, and avoiding overclaim (tags include 'Anti-Overclaim'), so results should be presented with verifiable artifacts for community scrutiny.
